findings.title: Public group members page only loads the first 50 users
findings.body: setupController always calls Group.findMembers(), and that method now always requests limit 50 (the new model default) and offset 0. The public members template (group/members.hbs) only iterates `members` and has no next/previous controls, unlike the admin group screen. Previously this endpoint returned every member of a non-automatic group and defaulted automatic groups to 200 when no limit was sent. After this change, any group with more than 50 members (including large custom groups and automatic groups such as trust_level_0) silently hides everyone past the first page, with no way to load the rest.

findings.title: totalPages is off by one when count is a multiple of page size
findings.body: totalPages is Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, which is wrong whenever user_count is greater than 0 and divisible by limit. A group of exactly 50 members with the default limit of 50 is reported as 2 pages, 100 members as 3, and so on. showingLast compares currentPage to that value, so Next stays enabled on the last real page. next() then sets offset to min(offset + limit, user_count), which equals user_count, and findMembers loads an empty page. Admins see a blank extra page and a wrong "N/M" indicator for every full page of members.

findings.title: Removing the last member on a page leaves a blank page
findings.body: findMembers clamps the request offset with Math.min(user_count, offset) using the in-memory user_count, which is only refreshed from the response. removeMember (and addMembers) then call findMembers() without moving offset back. Deleting the last user on the current page therefore re-requests an offset that is now past the end (the clamp still allows offset == old total). The server echoes that offset in meta and returns an empty members array, and the client stores meta.offset, so the admin UI stays on a blank page until Previous is clicked. The members action never clamps offset to the last non-empty page either.

findings.title: Remove control ignores whether the group is automatic
findings.body: This row is rendered by the group-member itemView, not in the admin group template's context. Ember's each+itemView sets the row context to the each keyword ({member: user}) or to the user record; neither has the group's automatic flag, and a replaced context does not fall back to the admin-group controller. {{#unless automatic}} is therefore always true, so the remove link is shown for automatic groups (admins, moderators, trust_level_*, and so on). Confirming still calls DELETE /admin/groups/:id/members, which correctly returns 422, but neither the removeMember action nor Group.removeMember handles the failure, so the admin gets a confirm dialog and then no error and no list refresh.

findings.title: Creating a group drops the chosen alias level
findings.body: create assigns name and visible, then saves, but never reads params[:alias_level]. The admin form shows the alias-level combo for new groups (it sits outside the {{#if id}} block), and Group.asJSON posts alias_level on create. update does apply alias_level, so editing an existing group works, but the first save always persists the default (0, nobody) no matter what was selected. The client only copies resp.basic_group.id back onto the model, so the UI keeps showing the unsaved choice until the group is reloaded. The new create spec only checks name stripping and would not catch this.

findings.title: Members limit and offset are unbounded and can 500
findings.body: The rewritten members action uses limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i and offset = params[:offset].to_i with no upper or lower bound. This route is available to anyone who can see the group, including public automatic groups that contain every user. A very large limit loads and serializes the entire membership in one request. A negative offset or limit is sent through to SQL; PostgreSQL rejects OFFSET/LIMIT < 0, so those query params 500 the endpoint. The old action at least defaulted automatic groups to 200; the rewrite should cap limit (and reject negative offset/limit) rather than trusting the client.

findings.title: GET /groups/:name/members.json response shape changed
findings.body: members used to render_serialized an array of GroupUserSerializer objects. It now returns an object {members, meta: {total, limit, offset}}. The in-repo Group.findMembers caller was updated, but this is a public route. Themes, plugins, and API clients that treated the body as an array (for example result.map or a JSON array decode) will break or show no members. There is no compat path, such as keeping the array when limit/offset are omitted, or a versioned response.

findings.title: No coverage for alias level or the new members payload
findings.body: The create example only posts a name and asserts stripping. Nothing asserts that alias_level from the flat params is persisted, which is the field create now ignores. There is also no spec for GroupsController#members, so the new {members, meta} contract, the default page size, and unbounded limit/offset are untested. The automatic remove example calls xhr :put, :remove_member while the route is DELETE; controller specs still invoke the action, so that mismatch does not fail CI and does not lock the route param (:group_id) either.
